transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer technical support, my name is Sophie. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Sophie. I am tearing my hair out here. My desktop Outlook program suddenly stopped downloading my work emails yesterday. It keeps popping up asking for my password over and over, and rejecting my correct password!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can check your email account settings. Let's start with security verification. What is your full name and the billing address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Dylan Hughes, 88 Cathedral Road, Cardiff, CF11 9LN.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what is the four-digit security PIN on your account, Dylan?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. And which software client and operating system are you having trouble with?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am running Microsoft Outlook 2019 on my Windows 11 desktop computer.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Are you able to log into webmail through your internet browser using that exact same password?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I logged into webmail on chrome twenty minutes ago and all my emails are sitting there, but Outlook on my PC rejects it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right. S-Net upgraded its email security platform on Monday to mandate two-factor authentication and dedicated App Passwords for third-party mail applications.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Nobody told me that! I've lost half a day's work trying to send customer estimates because of this surprise change! It is completely unacceptable!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We sent notification emails to all primary account holders three weeks prior to the migration.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well, I never saw it, and now my invoicing is completely stalled.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously third-party email clients like Outlook cannot handle two-factor push prompts directly, which is why a sixteen-character App Password must be generated.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fine, how do I generate this App Password then?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please open your web browser and go to my dot s-net dot co dot uk.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'm at the login screen.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Log in with your primary S-Net username and your regular master password.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Done. I am on the main account dashboard.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now click on the 'Security & Privacy' tab along the top navigation bar.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicked. It shows 'Password', 'Two-Factor Authentication', and 'App Passwords'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Click on 'Manage App Passwords'. Bear with me while your portal session token authenticates.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Dylan. Do you see the button that says 'Generate New App Password'?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I see the blue button.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Click that button, and enter the label 'Outlook Desktop' in the friendly name box.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Typed 'Outlook Desktop'. Now clicking Generate.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A sixteen-character code grouped in four blocks should appear on your screen.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it shows four blocks of four letters with hyphens.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Click the 'Copy to Clipboard' icon next to it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Copied.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let me check what application you are setting up again. Which email client software and version are you opening on your computer?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: As I told you at the beginning, it's Outlook 2019 on Windows 11.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, open Outlook 2019 on your desktop now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Outlook is open, and that little prompt box saying 'Enter your password for mail.s-net.co.uk' is sitting right in the center.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Clear out whatever is currently typed in the password field, right-click, and paste that sixteen-character App Password you copied.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Pasted the new password in.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Make sure the checkbox that says 'Remember password' is ticked, then click OK.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ticked remember password, clicking OK now...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Look at the bottom right corner of Outlook. Does it say 'Connected' or 'Send/Receive error'?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It says 'Connected to: mail.s-net.co.uk'... And the progress bar is moving... Wow, thirty-two new emails just poured into my inbox!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While we are in Outlook, what port number is showing under your outgoing server advanced settings?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It shows port 587 with STARTTLS encryption.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, port 587 is our secure authenticated submission port, so that's configured properly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, glad the port settings didn't get scrambled.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's fantastic news. Now let's test sending an email to make sure outgoing SMTP authentication is working properly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me send a test message to my personal Gmail account.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Take your time, let me know when the Outbox clears.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sent! Just checked my phone and the test email arrived in my Gmail inbox instantly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can you also confirm that your calendar and contacts synced up without error banners?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the yellow warning triangle at the bottom has disappeared completely.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm your email address on file, it's dylan dot hughes at s-net dot co dot uk, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's my main address.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm for our ticket notes, the account address is 88 Cathedral Road, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 88 Cathedral Road.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will leave this ticket reference open in your account notes in case you ever need to generate another token for a tablet or phone.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's very helpful, thank you Sophie.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Do you have any other technical questions about your email or webmail access today, Dylan?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, having Outlook working again saves my workday. Thank you for walking me through that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are very welcome. Thank you for choosing S-Net, Dylan, and have a productive day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Sophie, you too. Goodbye.
